images.caption: Figure 1:LongBananatask overview. (a) Each case pairs a heterogeneous reference set and structured synthesis prompt with the generated image under evaluation. (b)LongBanana-Eval converts graph-grounded checklist items into dimension-level scores and auditable evidence traces. The score labels Content, Relations, and Global denote Content Fidelity, Relational Binding, and Global Constraint Satisfaction, respectively.

Figure 2:The3×33\times 3taxonomy used to organizeLongBanana. Rows group cases into Scene Composition, Visual Appearance, and Reference Reasoning, while columns expose subclass-level demands used for diagnostic reporting. Each subclass contributes 10 cases.

Figure 3:LongBananaconstruction pipeline.(1) Scenario Construction: experts design scenarios aligned with the task taxonomy.(2) Graph Construction: an LLM structures each scenario into entities, attributes, relations, and whole-scene constraints.(3) Prompt & Reference Synthesis: the graph guides the creation of the target instruction and visual references.(4) Checklist & Curation: graph constraints are translated into evidence-linked checklist items, and human curators review the instruction, references, and checklist for consistency, visual feasibility, and verifiability.

Figure 4:LongBanana-Eval scoring pipeline. The parser assembles item-specific reference evidence and routes each check to one of three rubric critics. Critics inspect the evidence, call verification tools as needed, and return item labels with supporting traces. Item labels are averaged to produce dimension-level and overall scores.

Table 2:Harness and workflow comparison on the held-out 90-caseLongBananabenchmark. The foundation image model is fixed to Nano Banana 2, and the compared component is the generation harness/workflow. Subclass columns and Overall Avg. report the unweighted checklist-average score (0–100); P@70% is the difficulty-weighted task pass rate.Higher is better for all reported metrics.Boldface and underlining mark the best and second-best values in each column.

Table 3:Foundation image-model comparison on the same 90-caseLongBananabenchmark. The generation harness/workflow is fixed to OpenClaw + RPR, and the compared component is the foundation image model. Subclass columns and Overall Avg. use the same unweighted checklist-average score asTable2(0–100); P@70% is the difficulty-weighted task pass rate.Higher is better for all reported metrics.Boldface and underlining mark the best and second-best values in each column.

Figure 5:Human checklist annotation platform examples for count-oriented items. Top: acount_checkitem asks whether the target image contains exactly two luxury handbags, with the relevant handbag references, prompt, item question, scoring guidance, submitted score, and first-review approval visible in the same audit record. Bottom: acount_checkitem asks whether the full target image contains exactly four specified people, again tying the target output, references, item text, label submission and review result to a single checklist record.

Figure 6:Human checklist annotation platform example for a relation item. Therelation_checkscreen asks whether the warrior ally stands beside the protagonist, requiring the reviewer to compare the target image with the relevant character references and apply the predefined ternary labels. The stored record includes metadata, category, guidance text, submitted score, and first-review approval, supporting strict post-hoc audit of each checklist decision.
